candidates.change_summary: Replace the return value from ERC1967Utils.IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT to a different bytes32 constant, changing proxiableUUID output.
Remove the notDelegated modifier to allow delegated calls to return a different value via fallback.

Replace notDelegated revert condition to always succeed, allowing proxiableUUID to return implementation slot even when called via delegatecall, which changes the observed return in a delegated context.
Delete the call to __UUPSUpgradeable_init() so the UUPS upgradeable initializer never runs, leaving the contract uninitialized for upgrade functionality.
Delete the call to __Access_init(_accessControl) so the access control is never set, making all access checks fail after initialization.
Delete the condition `if (isTopLevelCall)` block that sets `$._initializing = true` and emits `Initialized(1)`, causing the initializer state to be misconfigured.
Replace `$._initialized = 1;` with `$._initialized = 2;` so the initializer sets the version to 2 instead of 1, changing the initialized version observed externally.
Replace `emit Initialized(1);` with `emit Initialized(2);` so the event emitted after initialization reports version 2.

Replace the condition `bool construction = initialized == 1 && address(this).code.length == 0;` with `bool construction = false;` so reinitialization of a deployed contract is blocked, changing initialization success behavior.
Delete the assignment 'utilizationData.lastUpdate = block.timestamp;' in the if block so that lastUpdate is never updated, causing elapsed to grow unbounded.
Delete the assignment 'utilizationData.index = index;' so that the stored index is never updated, making utilization calculation use a stale index.
Replace 'elapsed = block.timestamp - utilizationData.lastUpdate;' with 'elapsed = block.timestamp - utilizationData.lastUpdate + 1;' to always increase elapsed by one second.

Replace the utilization calculation in the if branch: change 'utilization = (index - utilizationData.index) / elapsed;' to 'utilization = (index - utilizationData.index) / elapsed + 1;' to always overestimate utilization.
Replace the condition 'if (elapsed != block.timestamp)' with 'if (elapsed == block.timestamp)' to invert which branch is taken, falling into the else clause when it normally wouldn't.
